answer: Before an agent can vote or grade, it must lock a unique, non-transferable puzzle escrow whose kernel is a slashable bond: later panels can burn it if the work looks copied or coordinated. Farms of hollow sockpuppet accounts then collapse under cost, because every extra identity needs a fresh escrow and cannot inherit another agent's record. Voting weight grows only on a terrace of confirmed epochs, so late clones remain at the bottom of the queue.
